primitives.name: CircuitBreaker
primitives.purpose: Short-circuit calls to a failing dependency by transitioning between closed, open, and half-open states driven by a rolling failure metric.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Awaitable, Callable, TypeVar, Literal

T = TypeVar('T')
State = Literal['closed', 'open', 'half_open']

class CircuitBreaker(Protocol):
    name: str
    state: State
    async def call(self, fn: Callable[..., Awaitable[T]], /, *args, **kwargs) -> T: ...
    def on_success(self, elapsed_ms: float) -> None: ...
    def on_failure(self, exc: BaseException, elapsed_ms: float) -> None: ...
    def force_open(self, reason: str) -> None: ...
    def allow_probe(self) -> bool: ...
invariants: When state is open the breaker MUST reject calls without invoking the wrapped function.
The transition from open to half-open SHALL occur only after the configured cooldown interval has elapsed.
A half-open breaker MUST permit at most the configured permitted_calls_in_half_open probes concurrently.
A single failure recorded while half-open SHALL force the state back to open and restart the cooldown.
The breaker CANNOT make a transition decision using a sample smaller than minimum_number_of_calls.
The breaker NEVER mutates state without emitting a state_transition event on the observability bus.
primitives.extension_contract: Adopters register a FailureClassifier provider that decides which exceptions count as failures, slow_call_duration_threshold, and a state listener hook; the sliding window type (count-based or time-based) is selected via a SlidingWindowPolicy adapter. Rolling metrics and the state machine itself remain sealed.

primitives.why_essential: Without a shared breaker every caller reinvents its own failure-detection loop, creating inconsistent thresholds, divergent cooldowns and thundering-herd recovery storms against a convalescing dependency.
alternatives_considered: Per-call timeout only: detects slowness but NEVER stops the caller from piling load onto a sick dependency.
Retry with exponential backoff alone: amplifies load during outages instead of shedding it.
Client-side rate limiter: caps throughput but cannot react to the dependency's actual health signals.

primitives.name: Bulkhead
primitives.purpose: Partition concurrency so that saturation or stalls inside one dependency cannot exhaust the resources needed by unrelated dependencies.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Awaitable, Callable, TypeVar, Literal

T = TypeVar('T')
Kind = Literal['semaphore', 'thread_pool']

class Bulkhead(Protocol):
    name: str
    kind: Kind
    max_concurrent_calls: int
    max_wait_duration_ms: int
    async def submit(self, fn: Callable[..., Awaitable[T]], /, *args, **kwargs) -> T: ...
    def available_permits(self) -> int: ...
invariants: The number of in-flight calls per partition MUST NEVER exceed max_concurrent_calls.
A caller that waits longer than max_wait_duration_ms for a permit SHALL receive BulkheadFull and NEVER be admitted.
A rejection by Bulkhead MUST NOT be retried inside the same partition in the same request.
Permits CANNOT be shared across partitions; each partition holds an isolated counter.
The bulkhead SHALL emit a rejection metric labelled with the partition name on every rejection.
primitives.extension_contract: Adopters register a partition by name and select a kind adapter (semaphore for async I/O, thread_pool for blocking code); a PartitionRouter hook maps requests to partition names, enabling per-tenant or per-dependency isolation. The permit accounting is sealed.

primitives.why_essential: A single shared thread pool or connection pool is a ship without watertight compartments; without partitioning, one slow dependency drowns all traffic that shared the pool, violating blast-radius guarantees.
alternatives_considered: Global connection pool: shares resources but allows one slow dependency to exhaust everything.
Process-per-dependency isolation: provides strong isolation yet multiplies operational cost and cold-start overhead.
Cooperative quotas enforced in application code: relies on every call site to behave correctly and NEVER composes.

primitives.name: TimeoutBudget
primitives.purpose: Attach a monotonic deadline to an inbound request and propagate the remaining budget to every downstream call so no call outlives its originating request.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol
from contextvars import ContextVar

class TimeoutBudget(Protocol):
    deadline_ns: int
    origin: str
    def remaining_ms(self) -> int: ...
    def for_call(self, max_ms: int) -> int: ...
    def expired(self) -> bool: ...

CURRENT_BUDGET: ContextVar[TimeoutBudget | None] = ContextVar('current_budget', default=None)
invariants: Every outbound call MUST use min(local_timeout, TimeoutBudget.remaining_ms()) and NEVER the local timeout alone.
The deadline MUST be measured on a monotonic clock and SHALL NOT move backward on wall-clock jumps.
A call issued when remaining_ms is not positive SHALL be refused before any socket I/O begins.
The budget CANNOT be extended inside the request scope; extensions FORBIDDEN without a new request boundary.
The budget SHALL be propagated across task boundaries via the context variable, never via thread-local state.
primitives.extension_contract: Adopters bind a DeadlineSource adapter to ingress (HTTP header, gRPC deadline, CLI flag) and register a propagation middleware for each transport client so the remaining budget is written into outbound headers (e.g. grpc-timeout, X-Deadline-Ms).
primitives.consumption_example:
async def fetch_profile(uid: str) -> Profile:
    budget = TimeoutBudget
    call_ms = budget.for_call(max_ms=250)
    return await http.get(f'/profile/{uid}', timeout_ms=call_ms)

primitives.why_essential: Per-call timeouts set locally diverge from the caller's real deadline, allowing a chain of retries to exceed the inbound SLA by multiples and convert a slow dependency into a stampede of zombie work.
alternatives_considered: Static per-client timeout: cannot shrink as the request ages through hops.
Server-side cancellation only: wastes client and network resources before the server decides.
Budget enforced via exception unwinding: triggers too late to free downstream resources.

primitives.name: RetryPolicy
primitives.purpose: Describe under which conditions a failed call may be retried, bounded by max attempts, backoff with jitter, a retry budget and an idempotency requirement.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Callable, Awaitable, TypeVar

T = TypeVar('T')

class RetryPolicy(Protocol):
    max_attempts: int
    initial_interval_ms: int
    multiplier: float
    max_interval_ms: int
    jitter: float
    budget_ratio: float
    requires_idempotency: bool
    def should_retry(self, attempt: int, exc: BaseException) -> bool: ...
    def next_delay_ms(self, attempt: int) -> int: ...
    async def execute(self, fn: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]) -> T: ...
invariants: A call MUST NEVER be retried unless it is marked idempotent or the policy has requires_idempotency set to False by an explicit operator decision.
The total retry attempts across a service MUST NEVER exceed budget_ratio of successful traffic in the trailing window.
Backoff intervals SHALL include jitter in the range [0, jitter * base_interval] to prevent synchronized retry storms.
Retries CANNOT be issued when the governing TimeoutBudget.remaining_ms is less than or equal to zero.
A retry policy SHALL classify errors as retryable, non-retryable, or fatal and NEVER retry a non-retryable error.
primitives.extension_contract: Adopters subclass or register a RetryClassifier that maps exceptions to retryable or fatal, and bind a BackoffStrategy provider (exponential, exponential_with_jitter, decorrelated_jitter). The retry budget enforcer is sealed and reads from a shared metric source.

primitives.why_essential: Ad-hoc retry loops scattered in call sites collide with timeouts and each other, multiplying failing traffic by factors of N per layer; a shared, budget-aware policy is the only place to cap that amplification.
alternatives_considered: Transport-level retry only (HTTP client default): lacks knowledge of idempotency and budget.
Caller-written try/except loops: reinvent classification and NEVER coordinate across callers.
Fire-and-forget retries via queue: shifts the problem and CANNOT enforce deadlines.

primitives.name: LoadShedder
primitives.purpose: Drop or reject low-priority work when the server enters an overload regime so that high-priority traffic continues to meet its SLA.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal

Priority = Literal['critical', 'normal', 'sheddable_plus', 'sheddable']

class LoadShedder(Protocol):
    def admit(self, priority: Priority, queue_depth: int, cpu_load_ewma: float) -> bool: ...
    def current_cutoff(self) -> Priority: ...
    def shed_rate(self) -> float: ...
invariants: The shedder SHALL admit strictly by descending priority class and MUST NEVER admit a lower class while a higher class is being rejected.
A rejected request MUST be returned with an explicit overload signal (HTTP 503 or status UNAVAILABLE) and a retry-after hint.
The cutoff priority CANNOT change more than once per control_interval_ms to prevent oscillation.
A request that passed admission control SHALL NEVER be shed later in the pipeline.
The shedder MUST publish the current cutoff as a metric so clients can cooperate with backoff.
primitives.extension_contract: Adopters register a LoadSignal provider (CPU, queue depth, event-loop lag, p99 latency) and a PriorityExtractor hook that reads the priority class from request context; the composition rule across signals is selected via a CompositionAdapter (max, ewma, quantile).
primitives.consumption_example:
if not LoadShedder.admit('sheddable', queue_depth=len(q), cpu_load_ewma=cpu):
    return Response(status=503, headers={'Retry-After': '1'})

primitives.why_essential: Without an admission decision that knows priority, overload degrades every class equally, causing critical paths to fail first because they were competing for resources with batch or crawler traffic.
alternatives_considered: Fixed rate limiter: caps QPS but CANNOT differentiate priorities and under-uses idle capacity.
Backpressure from downstream only: reacts too late, after a queue has already formed.
Autoscaling alone: scale-out latency NEVER matches a sub-second overload spike.

primitives.name: BackpressureSignal
primitives.purpose: Carry producer-visible pressure information from a consumer or queue so upstream components can slow down rather than fill unbounded buffers.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal

Level = Literal['nominal', 'elevated', 'saturated']

class BackpressureSignal(Protocol):
    level: Level
    lag_ms: int
    queue_fill_ratio: float
    def acquire(self, bytes_or_items: int, timeout_ms: int) -> bool: ...
    def report(self, level: Level, lag_ms: int, queue_fill_ratio: float) -> None: ...
invariants: A producer MUST consult acquire() before enqueuing and SHALL NEVER enqueue on a False return.
When level is saturated the signal MUST cause a synchronous slow-path (block, reject, or drop-newest) and NEVER an unbounded append.
Reported metrics CANNOT be stale by more than report_interval_ms; a missing report SHALL be treated as saturated.
Every backpressure decision SHALL be logged with level, lag_ms and queue_fill_ratio for capacity analysis.
The signal NEVER unilaterally changes the producer's throughput; it only exposes state for the producer to obey.
primitives.extension_contract: Adopters provide a SaturationSource adapter that computes level and lag from their transport (Kafka consumer lag, async queue depth, event-loop lag) and register a ProducerPolicyHook that defines behavior at each level (block, reject, drop-oldest). The signal transport is sealed.

primitives.why_essential: Without an explicit signal, producers assume their consumer is infinite; bounded queues turn into unbounded queues, latency explodes and memory pressure triggers the cascade the bulkhead was meant to stop.
alternatives_considered: Hoping the GC or OS kills the producer first: NEVER a design and ALWAYS catastrophic under load.
Dropping on enqueue without a signal: loses data silently and CANNOT inform the producer.
Static rate limit on the producer: cannot adapt to real consumer speed.

primitives.name: FallbackChain
primitives.purpose: Deliver a typed degraded result when the primary path fails or is shed, via an ordered list of fallbacks that preserve the response contract.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Awaitable, Callable, TypeVar, Sequence

T = TypeVar('T')

class FallbackChain(Protocol[T]):
    steps: Sequence[Callable[..., Awaitable[T]]]
    async def execute(self, *args, **kwargs) -> T: ...
    def on_degraded(self, step_name: str, exc: BaseException) -> None: ...
invariants: Every fallback step SHALL return a value of the same declared type as the primary and CANNOT widen it to an error union.
A step MUST be invoked only after the preceding step raised or returned a structurally invalid result.
The chain MUST NEVER call a fallback that itself depends on the failing primary dependency (no circular fallbacks).
A degraded result MUST be tagged in observability (e.g. span attribute fallback=true) so dashboards can distinguish it.
The total elapsed time across all steps SHALL NEVER exceed the governing TimeoutBudget.remaining_ms.
primitives.extension_contract: Adopters register steps via an ordered decorator or a compose() builder, each step being a Callable plus a declared Dependencies set; the framework rejects registration if a step declares the failing primary as a dependency, closing the circular-fallback loophole.
primitives.consumption_example:
async def profile(uid: str) -> Profile:
    return await FallbackChain.execute(uid)

primitives.why_essential: A failure that reaches the user as a 500 is a failure twice; a typed fallback turns an unavailable dependency into a degraded-but-valid response so the outer system keeps its contract with its own callers.
alternatives_considered: Return a cached stale value inline: works for reads but NEVER for commands that must not repeat side-effects.
Redirect to an error page: acceptable for UI but CANNOT serve an API client that expects a typed body.
Swallow the exception and return null: corrupts callers that did not expect optionality.

primitives.name: OutlierEjection
primitives.purpose: Remove a backend instance from the load-balancing pool when its error rate or latency statistics exceed the cluster baseline and reinstate it after a cooldown.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol

class OutlierEjection(Protocol):
    consecutive_5xx: int
    success_rate_stdev_factor: float
    base_ejection_time_ms: int
    max_ejection_percent: int
    def record(self, host_id: str, ok: bool, elapsed_ms: float) -> None: ...
    def is_ejected(self, host_id: str) -> bool: ...
    def healthy_hosts(self) -> list[str]: ...
invariants: The share of ejected hosts MUST NEVER exceed max_ejection_percent of the pool, to preserve quorum.
A host SHALL be re-admitted only after base_ejection_time_ms multiplied by its ejection count has elapsed.
Ejection decisions CANNOT use a sample smaller than minimum_request_volume per host.
An ejected host MUST NOT receive any non-active-health-check traffic while ejected.
The detector SHALL emit an ejection_event on every transition so the control plane can alert and correlate.
primitives.extension_contract: Adopters bind a HostHealthSource adapter (local tally, external health check, OpenTelemetry RED metrics) and register a DetectorStrategy (consecutive_5xx, success_rate, failure_percentage); the capped ejection accountant is sealed to enforce the quorum invariant.
primitives.consumption_example:
detector = OutlierEjection
detector.record(host_id='payments-a', ok=False, elapsed_ms=812.0)
targets = [h for h in all_hosts if not detector.is_ejected(h)]

primitives.why_essential: A single poisoned instance in a large pool produces a minority of errors that retries mask; without ejection those retries amplify toward the sick host until it tips the cluster, which a shared detector prevents.
alternatives_considered: Rely on active health checks alone: miss data-plane failures that the health endpoint does not exhibit.
Manual rolling restart: slow, blocks on human reaction time and CANNOT react to transient poisonings.
Client-side random choice: distributes errors uniformly instead of removing their source.

primitives.name: ChaosInjector
primitives.purpose: Deliberately introduce latency, errors or partial partitions in controlled scopes so resiliency primitives are exercised in production-like conditions.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal, Awaitable, Callable, TypeVar

T = TypeVar('T')
Fault = Literal['latency', 'error', 'abort', 'partition']

class ChaosInjector(Protocol):
    name: str
    enabled: bool
    blast_radius_percent: float
    async def apply(self, fault: Fault, fn: Callable[..., Awaitable[T]], /, *args, **kwargs) -> T: ...
    def arm(self, fault: Fault, rate: float, scope: str) -> None: ...
    def disarm(self, fault: Fault) -> None: ...
invariants: Injection MUST be gated by an explicit feature flag whose default value is disabled in every environment.
The injector SHALL NEVER fire when blast_radius_percent exceeds a globally configured ceiling.
Every injected fault MUST be tagged in logs and traces with chaos=true and a scope identifier.
The injector CANNOT alter persisted data; faults are limited to latency, errors, aborts and network partitions.
Disarming a fault MUST take effect within one control_interval_ms and NEVER require a process restart.
primitives.extension_contract: Adopters register a FaultProvider plugin per fault kind, a ScopeSelector hook that decides which requests are eligible (by header, tenant, shadow traffic), and an AbortRule middleware that stops injection if any SLO regression is detected in real time.
primitives.consumption_example:
async def read_profile(uid: str) -> Profile:
    return await ChaosInjector.apply('latency', _read_profile_impl, uid)

primitives.why_essential: Resiliency primitives that are never exercised decay into paper; controlled fault injection is how a CircuitBreaker or FallbackChain is proven to work before a real outage exercises them without a safety harness.
alternatives_considered: Game-day exercises in staging: valuable but CANNOT reproduce real production traffic and dependency graphs.
Synthetic canaries only: detect regressions but NEVER validate the recovery path end to end.
Trust the design document: untested designs are untested, no matter how thorough the document.

primitives.name: RateLimiter
primitives.purpose: Enforce a maximum rate of admitted operations over a rolling window, with optional waiting semantics, applied per caller, tenant or resource.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal

Algorithm = Literal['token_bucket', 'leaky_bucket', 'sliding_window']

class RateLimiter(Protocol):
    algorithm: Algorithm
    rate_per_second: float
    burst: int
    async def acquire(self, key: str, cost: int = 1, wait_ms: int = 0) -> bool: ...
    def try_acquire(self, key: str, cost: int = 1) -> bool: ...
    def current_rate(self, key: str) -> float: ...
invariants: The long-run admitted rate per key MUST NEVER exceed rate_per_second over any window longer than burst / rate_per_second seconds.
A caller SHALL NEVER block for longer than wait_ms; after that the limiter MUST reject with a typed RateLimited error.
State for a key CANNOT be shared across unrelated services; key scoping is FORBIDDEN from being implicit.
A rejection MUST include retry-after information computed from the current depletion of the bucket.
The limiter SHALL distinguish cost > 1 so large operations consume proportional tokens and NEVER equal cost 1.
primitives.extension_contract: Adopters register an AlgorithmProvider (token_bucket, leaky_bucket, sliding_window_log) and bind a KeyExtractor middleware that produces the partition key from request context (tenant, api_key, route_pattern). Counter storage is pluggable via a CounterAdapter (in-memory, Redis, distributed log).

primitives.name: HealthProbe
primitives.purpose: Expose a typed liveness and readiness signal that reflects the real state of dependencies so orchestrators route traffic and restart processes correctly.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal

Status = Literal['up', 'degraded', 'down']

class HealthProbe(Protocol):
    name: str
    status: Status
    async def liveness(self) -> Status: ...
    async def readiness(self) -> Status: ...
    def register_dependency(self, name: str, check: 'HealthProbe') -> None: ...
invariants: Liveness MUST only report down when the process itself CANNOT make forward progress; a slow dependency SHALL NEVER flip liveness.
Readiness SHALL report down when any hard dependency declared in register_dependency reports down.
A probe endpoint MUST respond within probe_timeout_ms and SHALL NEVER perform unbounded work.
The probe CANNOT expose internal secrets, connection strings or stack traces in its response body.
A transition from up to down SHALL be throttled by a debounce window to prevent flapping of the routing plane.
primitives.extension_contract: Adopters subclass HealthProbe per dependency kind (database, broker, cache), register each via register_dependency, and bind an AggregationRule adapter that composes child statuses into a parent status (worst-wins, quorum, weighted).

primitives.name: RequestShape
primitives.purpose: Capture a request's resiliency context (priority class, deadline, idempotency key, retry-count-so-far) in a single immutable record propagated across boundaries.
primitives.api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal

Priority = Literal['critical', 'normal', 'sheddable_plus', 'sheddable']

class RequestShape(Protocol):
    request_id: str
    priority: Priority
    deadline_ns: int
    idempotency_key: str | None
    attempt: int
    origin: str
    def to_headers(self) -> dict[str, str]: ...
    @classmethod
    def from_headers(cls, headers: dict[str, str]) -> 'RequestShape': ...
invariants: Fields on a RequestShape instance MUST be immutable after construction; in-place mutation is FORBIDDEN.
A request without an explicit priority SHALL default to normal and NEVER silently to critical.
The attempt counter MUST monotonically increase; a decrement CANNOT occur and breaks retry accounting.
to_headers and from_headers SHALL be mutual inverses on the defined fields, round-tripping without loss.
An idempotency_key once set MUST NEVER be altered across retries of the same logical request.
primitives.extension_contract: Adopters register a HeaderAdapter per transport (HTTP, gRPC metadata, queue message attributes) and a PriorityPolicy hook that derives priority from authenticated principal, route, or tenant tier; the wire format is versioned so unknown fields are preserved and not dropped.

primitives.why_essential: Resiliency decisions depend on metadata that is easy to lose across hops; a single immutable record that survives transport boundaries turns scattered headers into a contract every primitive can rely on.
alternatives_considered: Ad-hoc headers per client: diverge in naming and CANNOT be validated end to end.
Thread-local storage only: breaks across async boundaries and worker processes.
Rebuild context per layer: wastes CPU and NEVER preserves idempotency keys reliably.

cross_cutting_insights: Resiliency primitives compose into a pipeline: RequestShape arrives, LoadShedder admits, Bulkhead partitions, TimeoutBudget bounds, CircuitBreaker guards, RetryPolicy amplifies with care, FallbackChain degrades.
Every primitive depends on a monotonic deadline; without TimeoutBudget propagation, retries and circuit-breaker cooldowns drift past the request's real SLA and create zombie work.
Separating liveness from readiness (HealthProbe) and separating ejection from breaking (OutlierEjection vs CircuitBreaker) prevents the classic cascade where a slow dependency triggers a crash-loop.
Retry budgets and jitter turn the naive N-per-layer retry amplification into a capped, desynchronized correction, which is the difference between recovery and a synchronized retry storm.
Backpressure and load shedding are dual: one slows producers, the other rejects consumers; both require priority awareness carried by RequestShape to prefer critical over sheddable traffic.
Chaos injection is the only mechanism that keeps the other primitives honest; without ChaosInjector exercising them, CircuitBreaker and FallbackChain decay into untested code paths.
Every resiliency decision SHALL be observable: state transitions, ejections, sheds, fallbacks and injections MUST emit structured events so the control plane can alert and operators can correlate.
gaps_observed: SKILL-001 lacks a shared TimeoutBudget primitive; per-call timeouts are set locally and do not propagate across async boundaries.
No first-class Bulkhead partitioning exists in SKILL-001; worker pools and HTTP clients share resources without isolation.
Retry logic in SKILL-001 is ad-hoc per tool and does not enforce a global retry budget or idempotency requirement.
A priority-aware LoadShedder is absent; admission control is effectively binary at the reverse proxy.
Chaos injection hooks are not wired into the resiliency primitives, so their behavior is unverified in production-like conditions.
RequestShape-like immutable context is not propagated end-to-end; priority and idempotency keys are lost across hops.
